Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied finished square three-panel watercolor illustration with ONLY TWO kinds of changes.

1. Open the framing of the TOP and MIDDLE panels: uniformly zoom out each ENTIRE scene by approximately 35% and show the floor under its worktable, so BOTH seated adult characters have their entire continuous bodies, natural seated hips-to-legs connection, TWO complete lower legs and TWO feet visible INSIDE the panel, like the already correctly framed bottom panel. Show the complete worktable with its tabletop and legs, full chairs as much as visible, and all important objects within the panel. Keep the overall square canvas and the THREE stacked panels in their existing positions/heights; do not reduce or move the bottom panel. Extend the current room/floor wash naturally within each top panel after zooming out. Bodies retain the SAME medium neutral adult proportions as the bottom characters, never squashed or stretched or childlike; heads remain PERFECT CIRCLES. Keep blue on LEFT and yellow on RIGHT, same seated poses, faces, eyes, pointing hand in TOP, blue's worried hand at head and yellow's helping hand in MIDDLE, identical cream straight aprons and each red-cloth THREAD TANGLE. Do not just append detached legs to cropped torsos. Maintain connected plausible seated anatomy under the table. Keep the THREE dialogue bubbles clearly readable and belonging to their existing speaker.

2. In the BOTTOM panel ONLY: remove the unintended Persian slogan «کار بهتر با هم» and its heart symbol from the small paper on the rear wall between/right of the characters. Replace the contents of that one paper with a plain tiny garment-sewing pattern sketch: simple thin pencil-like outline of a sleeve and a dotted seam, NO writing, NO numbers, NO heart. Keep the same paper, clip, location, watercolor and surrounding wall. No other bottom-panel change.

Absolute invariants: bottom panel remains visually identical except the contents of that one wall paper. Keep lower full feet/chairs/table, room, sewing props, mannequins, fabric basket, blue/yellow anatomy and eyes, small thread tangle on red fabric, their calm joint action and bubble. Preserve the blue's TOP thought bubble of banknotes and the entire narrative order: impatient blue blames yellow; blue receives yellow's patience; blue later behaves patiently toward yellow. No new speech, instructions, symbols, captions, people or events. All existing THREE spoken texts remain verbatim, in the same panels and attached to the same speaker: TOP BLUE «باز گره خورد؟!»; MIDDLE YELLOW «آروم، درستش می‌کنیم.»; BOTTOM BLUE «با هم درستش می‌کنیم.» Correct connected colloquial Persian only; absolutely no other writing.

Preserve the existing strong book style exactly: real moderate layered translucent hand-painted watercolor INSIDE all heads/bodies, paper, gentle irregular washes, darker LOCAL body-color contours, soft head/shoulder contact shadow; no flat/vector/marker/colored-pencil grain, glossy 3D or heavy mottling. Same small dark oval eyes with tiny inner glints where present, never white sclera. Same few fine short yellow eyelashes on the original eye structure; do not enlarge or alter eyes. Neutral medium adult forms, no feminine chest, pinched waist or hip/buttock bulges, no extra clothing beyond current matching straight cream aprons. Visible hands three fingers plus one thumb with natural grip occlusion. Keep clean white gutters and irregular watercolor margins, with all complete feet and props safely inside each panel.

seed.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a NEW square narrative book illustration, not a copy of either reference scene. Input image 1 (97): reference ONLY for medium adult neutral full-body proportions, simple eyes and local-colored contours. Input image 2 (131): reference ONLY for genuine layered watercolor, luminous pigment and paper; disregard its scene and sharp blush. Match this existing book's painterly visual identity. Broad overlapping translucent watercolor washes visible INSIDE heads, torsos, limbs and hands, gentle pigment pooling, restrained hand-painted texture; no marker, colored-pencil grain, flat vector, glossy/3D paint. Heads are PERFECT CIRCLES, width equals height, no oval, chin, jaw, ears, nose, hair or neck. Medium balanced adult neutral bodies, modest arms, not skinny or chunky; female bodies identical to other bodies, no breast, narrow waist, hip or buttock bulge, indentations. Gender if needed only a few short fine upper-outer eyelashes on the SAME small dark oval eyes. Tiny internal white glints allowed; NO surrounding white sclera. No sharp circular pink cheeks: either omit blush or extremely faint diffuse watercolor. Outlines are darker shades of each body's own color, never black body outlines. Soft local-color crescent contact shadow under each round head joining shoulders directly. Visible hands have THREE fingers PLUS ONE thumb, normal natural grips. Every foot and important prop fully INSIDE the image, no accidental clipping. Generous irregular watercolor edges with clean white paper margins. All writing ONLY short correctly connected colloquial Persian; no English. Family-friendly, warm, gentle human wit. Read scenes right-to-left then downward, thin WHITE gutters, no heavy frames. Calm uncluttered composition for an ADULT audience, not preschool/chibi.
Three wide stacked narrative panels inside a square, warm restrained adult sewing workshop. BLUE adult tailor is primary; LEMON-YELLOW adult junior coworker, NOT a child. Both balanced neutral bodies in matching simple straight cream aprons, no gendered silhouettes and no additional clothes. Minimal sewing machine and ordinary cloth on large worktable, full seated feet visible beneath table. A distinctive messy loose dark thread tangle on red fabric is the repeated challenge; make it realistic and small, not a monster.
TOP, beginning of work: blue impatiently points to yellow's tangled thread, harsh eyebrows and small speech «باز گره خورد؟!» Yellow looks discouraged with hands near fabric. Blue has a SMALL thought bubble of just banknotes; concern for output/income dominates. No money labels elsewhere. No needles pointed at anyone.
MIDDLE, during work: BLUE's own red fabric has the SAME kind of tangle. Blue stops, frustrated and then embarrassed; YELLOW sits beside blue and gently holds the thread with natural three-fingers-plus-thumb hands, compassionate eyes, saying «آروم، درستش می‌کنیم.» Blue visibly receives patience, not a technical sewing lesson. No instructional arrows, diagrams or miraculous new machine; the workplace difficulty reveals human vulnerability.
BOTTOM, later: yellow again has a thread tangle; now BLUE moves own chair next to yellow and calmly helps untangle with a warm smile, no pointing or blame, short speech «با هم درستش می‌کنیم.» Yellow brightens and relaxes. Both full lower bodies naturally aligned with seated torsos; no twisted feet, feminine waist or bust. Keep blue/yellow identities and same small tools continuous. This is a more patient and humble PERSON formed by work experience, not simply a more skilled seamstress or a recipient of more money. No diploma/trophy. Soft humor in the boss learning patience from the junior adult. Only the three quoted short Persian lines, natural joined Persian. Real layered watercolor and white irregular paper margins.

fullGenerationPromptEnglish:
Create one finished square 1:1 narrative watercolor illustration for an adult and teenage visual book. Arrange THREE full-width horizontal scenes stacked from top to bottom with thin white gutters and no heavy comic frames. Tell a simple causal story in a warm sewing workshop: a BLUE adult tailor initially thinks of income and impatiently blames a YELLOW adult coworker for tangled thread; blue then experiences the same difficulty and receives yellow's patient help; later blue treats yellow with the patience learned during the work. The change must be visible in treatment of the person, not merely in improved sewing technique. Use only these two consistent characters in every scene. The emotional tone is gentle and humane, with quiet wit in the demanding tailor learning patience from the coworker.

HAND-PAINTED BOOK STYLE
Use real moderate watercolor on textured white paper. Broad translucent overlapping washes and gentle variations of pigment are visible throughout the HEADS, TORSOS, ARMS, LEGS and HANDS, not only at the background edges. Preserve luminous lighter areas with paper showing through and a little soft pigment pooling at natural painted edges. BLUE is shaded with transparent cyan and blue washes, with darker blue contours; YELLOW uses warm lemon and golden washes, with darker ocher contours. Never outline the bodies with black. Use small dark facial marks, soft local-color contact shadows beneath the heads, and quiet floor and chair shadows. The room uses warm peach and cream, light wood, a restrained multicolored rug and soft green plants. No flat vector fills, marker coloring, colored-pencil grain, glossy plastic, heavily mottled paint or airbrushed 3D shading. Blush is omitted or an extremely faint blended watercolor wash, never a sharp circular pink cheek. Natural organic outer paint edges remain inside generous white paper margins. Keep all three rows fully framed, with every seated lower leg, foot and important table support inside its own scene, never clipped at the gutter.

CHARACTER STRUCTURE AND CONTINUITY
Blue and yellow are neutral, medium, balanced ADULT figures with simple almost straight-sided torsos, modest arms and naturally connected seated hips, knees, lower legs and rounded feet. Neither is very thin, chunky, baby-like or chibi. Yellow is a junior adult coworker, not a child. Both genders use the SAME neutral body shape, with no breasts, pinched waist, protruding hips or buttocks, or feminine bulges and indentations. Both wear matching plain straight CREAM aprons with simple shoulder straps and a small rectangular front pocket, and no other clothes. Heads are PERFECT CIRCLES, equal width and height, with no elongated oval, pointed chin, jaw, ears, nose, hair or separate neck. The round head joins the shoulders directly with a soft darker same-color crescent shadow, keeping its boundary clear. Use the same small dark oval eyes on both characters. Tiny white glints INSIDE the dark eyes are allowed; white sclera around them is forbidden. If yellow has a few fine SHORT upper-outer eyelashes, attach them to the existing small eye shape without widening, whitening or restyling the eye. Simple eyebrows and mouth convey discouragement, frustration and later kindness. Closed happy arc eyes are suitable for yellow in the last scene. Each hand has THREE fingers PLUS ONE thumb, with natural grips and genuine occlusion when handling fine thread. Hands, arms and seated lower bodies connect believably. Keep blue consistently on the LEFT and yellow on the RIGHT in all scenes.

REPEATED WORKPLACE AND PROPS
The same warm workshop has a light wooden floor and pale peach textured walls. A long ordinary brown wooden worktable is seen from the front. Scale the complete table and people together so its tabletop, supports, two wooden chairs and BOTH feet of EACH seated worker fit within every row, with floor space visible beneath them. A restrained red, violet and orange patterned rug lies below the table. Blue sits at the left and yellow at the right. A recognizably red length of fabric runs across the tabletop and drapes over the right edge. Dark fine thread forms small believable messy tangles on this cloth. The SAME kind of tangle is repeated across scenes as the shared difficulty. It is not a monster, magical knot, knot diagram or oversized emblem.
Ordinary sewing tools include folded green, blue and purple cloth at the left, a red round pincushion with a few pin heads, blue-handled scissors, a small spool where appropriate, and a cream mug holding scissors or pencils at the right. Keep pins safely in the cushion and scissors resting on the table. Behind the characters, show a simple pale blue sewing machine on a smaller rear wooden bench. At the right is a large wooden-framed window with soft green foliage outside and a potted plant. At the left are shelves with bolts or folded rolls of colored cloth, a few drawers and trailing greenery. A woven cloth basket with neatly folded fabric sits near the window. The wall carries a few clipped simple garment outlines, all WITHOUT text, letters or numbers. These details establish work and remain subordinate to the faces, hands and repeated red fabric problem.

TOP SCENE: IMPATIENT BLAME
The BLUE tailor sits at the LEFT, with the whole seated body, both feet and chair safely visible below the table. Blue has angled impatient eyebrows, small dark oval eyes and a slightly open frowning mouth. One arm points accusingly across the red fabric toward YELLOW's small tangled thread; the other rests near the work. A white speech bubble belongs clearly to blue and reads EXACTLY: "باز گره خورد؟!". Above and slightly to the left of blue is a separate small thought cloud containing a bundled stack of green banknotes with a pale band and simple money shapes, but NO writing or digits. It shows the initial focus on income and output without filling the scene with wealth symbols.
YELLOW sits on the RIGHT, complete from round head to both feet, looking discouraged with softly raised inner eyebrows and a small downturned mouth. Yellow holds a fine strand of thread near the little tangle on the red cloth. The red fabric runs from left of center across the table and drapes over the right edge. A red spool is near blue, with scissors and folded fabric further left and the cream tool mug at the right. The workshop shelves, window, machine, rug and table supports are all in view. Do not add extra dialogue, punishment or a threatening gesture.

MIDDLE SCENE: RECEIVING PATIENCE IN THE SAME DIFFICULTY
At the same table, the BLUE tailor has now met the SAME small thread tangle on the red fabric in front of blue. Blue's harshness has disappeared: the round face looks worried or embarrassed, with soft upturned inner eyebrows and a small uncertain mouth. One hand rests against the side of the head, expressing frustration; a modest unlettered dark scribble above the head can convey that frustration. The money thought cloud is absent.
YELLOW remains at the RIGHT, leaning a little toward blue's work with a calm concerned expression. Yellow gently works with the fine thread near the small knot and offers patient help. A white speech bubble clearly belonging to yellow reads EXACTLY: "آروم، درستش می‌کنیم.". This is a kind response to another person's difficulty, rather than a technical demonstration of a special sewing method. Show blue recognizing that help. The repeated red cloth and small thread knot make the experience visually related to the first scene. Keep both people at the same scale with connected seated legs and both full feet visible. The complete wooden table and chair supports fit in the painted area. Maintain the same simple workshop background and tools, without instructional arrows or explanatory captions.

BOTTOM SCENE: RETURNING THE LEARNED PATIENCE
In the same workshop a little later, BLUE and YELLOW sit closer together at the worktable, blue on the LEFT and yellow on the RIGHT. YELLOW is again working on a small tangle in the red cloth. Now BLUE calmly reaches toward the thread to help, with a warm curved smile and relaxed eyebrows, replacing the earlier pointing and blame. Blue's hands and yellow's hands are naturally near the small thread tangle, showing gentle shared attention rather than a lesson in machinery. Yellow's face relaxes into a warm smile, with simple closed happy arc eyes if useful. A single white bubble belongs to BLUE and reads EXACTLY: "با هم درستش می‌کنیم.". No money thought cloud or scribble remains. The visible outcome is blue's changed patience toward the coworker, not a trophy, certificate, extra payment or a new skill emblem.
This lower scene is fully framed: the table's full legs, both chairs as visible, naturally aligned lower bodies and all FOUR feet sit within the panel above the clean white border. The red cloth drapes softly over the right tabletop edge. Keep folded fabric, pincushion and resting scissors on the left and the cream tool mug on the right. At far left a simple neutral sewing mannequin on a complete wooden stand has a soft blue cloth draped over one shoulder, with no human face. Near the window at far right are several tall colored fabric rolls and the woven cloth basket. The same warm rug and pale wooden floor extend below the table.
On the rear wall to the right of the workers is one clipped plain cream paper showing only a small garment-outline or sleeve sewing pattern with a dotted seam. This paper has NO words, slogan, heart, letters, digits or caption. Other small wall sheets also contain only quiet outline sketches. Keep the surrounding workshop inviting and restrained rather than turning the paper into a message board.

TEXT AND FINAL CHECKS
The ONLY writing anywhere in the illustration is the THREE quoted short Persian speech lines, naturally joined and clearly legible, one in each scene and attached to the specified speaker. No English text, numbers, labels, signature, watermark, banner or moralizing slogan. Preserve the three-row visual sequence: blue points and blames while imagining money, blue receives kind help when facing the same knot, blue later offers the same patience. Do not alter the eye structure to suggest gender, exaggerate the bodies, elongate the circular heads or omit the watercolor layering within them. Keep generous white outer margins, thin white gutters, full legs and feet, complete table supports and natural restrained human emotion in every scene.
